For the final day of the spring sale there are a ton of new sales. I'm not going to cover all the games on sale, since they have a ton, but I'll pick some that I feel strongly about from each day.

Jazzpunk
A short game with a series of spy missions that have a wacky sense of humor. There are a lot of things to play with but I'm not sure that you can actually lose - it's definitely more of an experience than a challenge. I enjoyed it for what it was though.

 

Eldritch
This little first-person dungeon crawler has a pretty good feel - I just wish it had a bigger selection of items, and didn't force you to regear every time you die. Luckily there is a loot-heavy bonus mode that you can use to get your favorite items back pretty quickly.

It could use one extra utility slot too - I rarely had space to carry the interesting special items.

 

Master Reboot
I liked this abstract dream world - it kept me interested the entire time and had a nice mix of puzzles, exploration, and a tiny bit of combat. I think it was a bit on the short side, but for $2.99 it's definitely worth checking out in my opinion.

 

Cube & Star
This game is mostly just rolling your cube around, exploring and interacting with the world - there isn't much in the way of instruction. There's a decent amount of content here though, if you can figure it out, including a narrative in a completely different language which you can slowly decipher.

I'm not sure if enjoy is the right word, but it was a unique experience.

 

Retro Game Crunch
This is actually a bundle of a few different games, and although they're all short - a couple hours at best - some of them were pretty cool.

I liked the one where you explore and evolve into different animals best - but there are a bunch of genres here. A couple of them probably won't interest most people, but if you like retro style graphics there's probably something you'll enjoy in here.

 

Our Darker Purpose
A solid Binding Of Isaac type game, without the puerile thematic content. It wasn't spectacularly interesting, but I didn't find any major issues with it either. So if you're looking for less crass game of that type this might be an option.

 

Vessel
This puzzle-platformer focuses a lot of physics and liquid simulations, and I felt like the platforming and playing a character detracted a bit from the puzzle part. The story is decent though, so the character isn't a total waste, and it has a solid graphical style.

Overall not a game I loved, but if you like puzzle-platfomers this one is okay.

 

Paper Sorcerer
A turn-based dungeon crawler, with a 4 character party. This can be pretty difficult in places, and I wish it had been far more balanced. It does have a save function though, so if you use that regularly these balance issues won't be quite so frustrating.

It did have some weird battle mechanics - like enemies with a huge amount of defense that isn't shown in the stats. Taking out those guys can be a bit repetitive.

 

Super Splatters
The tutorial and unlocking moves took a bit too long for my tastes - but doing stunts and exploding piles off goo was kind of fun. I wish the fluid mechanics had been done better though - for a game that's all about splashing liquid around it's crucial that this works properly. And unfortunately it didn't flow through the goal areas in a satisfying way.

 

A Wizard's Lizard
A Binding-of-Isaac type game where you have to kill yourself to progress through certain areas of the levels. If you die when you're in ghost form you lose.

Certain items like health bars for enemies really should be default - but once you unlock them you can buy them before the start of each game. Because of this starting gear mechanic the game becomes easier over time - and you'll probably need this better equipment to actually beat it.

It isn't really about doing more damage - the weapons just have different ranges and attack types - so you have to find one that caters to your play style. There are a few frustrating elements of the combat, but for the most part it was a pretty solid game.

 

Solar 2
A short solar system game, where you start as a small asteroid and crash into other objects to gain mass - eventually sucking in planets and other galactic objects. There are a bunch of optional missions that are pretty hard, which add a lot more content - but I enjoyed just growing my planet the most.

 

Machinarium
This point-and-click has a lot of difficult puzzles, not very intuitive in my opinion. It also doesn't distinguish well between background and usable items, which makes solving it even harder. Not bad, but you really have to enjoy point-and-click puzzles to avoid being frustrated by it.

 

Blocks That Matter
A platformer where you drill and collect blocks and then place them down in Tetris shapes to use as stairs, etc. Unfortunately there's no reverse time ability so if you make a mistake you often have to restart the entire level over.

 

Walking Dead
Obviously this series is known for having a good story - it's basically a choose your own adventure game with point-and-click elements. The downside is that a lot of your choices have no real relevance to the story - often they just choose which of your companions is present during the journey, not what actually happens.

This lack of actual choice was a bit disappointing, but the story is still interesting - so if linearity doesn't bother you it may still be worth a look.

 

Darksiders
The world in this hack-n-slash is pretty cool, and the weapons are satisfying. It is quite linear, but they designed it well enough that it doesn't feel like a corridor - and I actually got a good Legend Of Zelda vibe from it. If you like those type of games this series might be worth a look.

 

Red Faction Collection
I've only played Red Faction 1 and Armageddon, but the whole series is really known for how destructible the environments are in the games. The first one is quite old and pretty innovative in that respect, you can tunnel through most of the rock in the game using your weapons.

Armageddon prevents terrain destruction but even massive buildings can be knocked down, and it's pretty cool to see - although the camera is a tight-third person view like console games. That makes it a bit more annoying than it should be.

The enemies in this game are pretty easy, and in many places you can just run past them until you hit one of the numerous cutscenes (which despawns everything chasing you). Weapons are also limited, 4 slots. It's very obviously a console experience, and has a lot of strange design decisions that seem more like they were focused on the technical aspects of the game instead of making sure it was fun.

I don't know what barrel is pretty worn means. Most .45 ACP's that have been shot a lot are still in pretty good shape. The copper FMJ projectiles at 850-900 fps just don't wear much. The rifling of a .45 ACP was pretty shallow to begin with. The other wear points are the barrel bushing, (sloppy when new was normal) the barrel locking cam, (under the barrel just forward of the chamber) This should force the barrel up into the locking recesses in the slide, and the barrel tang at the upper end of the chamber. This tang rides in a slot in the slide. It can be a loose fit but it shouldn't expose the base of the cartridge case. (The Old .45 ACP was a low pressure cartridge as the base of the cartridge was unsupported and any high pressure blew out the bottom of the case.) JD

This sub will take a bit of time to get up and running so I wanted to quickly say hello to anyone that is wandering by. I would also like to share a bit of what we would like this new subverse to be all about!

There is an awful lot of misinformation out there regarding our pet hedgehogs and their care...the Reddit sub can be especially bad for that so I wanted to create an online community where people can come to get accurate information on how to care for their hedgehog. If you already own one of these little dudes then you know that they do take a bit of extra care.

With their popularity rising due to exposure on various social media sites also comes a sharp increase in hedgehogs being taken to shelters for surrender and being sold on places like Craigslist. Backyard breeders are popping up at an alarming rate and most of them have zero information as to the hedgehog's health pedigree. They simply buy a male and female and off they go. The mortality rate for these babies tends to be high as hedgehog mamas get agitated easily and then eat or injure their little ones. There are genetic diseases that are being passed down instead of being decreased by careful selective breeding. I would like to make it clear that this sort of breeding is NOT supported on this sub.

This will be a place to come with your questions about diet, housing, general maintenance, what to expect when you have to take your little guy to the vet, pretty much everything concerning hedgehog welfare. I'd also like this to be a place for volunteers that do rescue work, foster care, etc. whether it be with an organization (such as the Hedgehog Welfare Society or the IHA) or as a personal passion to share information and contacts. The Hedgehog Welfare Society in particular does excellent work with hedgehogs through the US and a little bit in Canada too. More rescue stations are needed, though, as are people willing to help out with hedgehog transport, pick-up and the like. You don't have to actually house a hedgehog in order to help out.

Along with having a rescue station or doing foster care comes the need to know basic first aid for hedgehogs. Not everyone has access to a 24-hour emergency vet. There are many things that can be done at home to keep your hedgehog comfortable until you can get into a clinic so this information will be here for you in case of emergencies. As this sub grows I hope that there will be a good deal of input and tips from current hedgehog guardians. After the emergency has been dealt with you may have a sick little hedgehog to look after. Maybe they aren't able to eat on their own and/or have mobility issues. There are several good food recipes that I would like to share that are excellent for syringe-feeding and have proven to successfully maintain and increase weight.

Lastly, there is a terrible disease called Wobbly Hedgehog Syndrome that is fairly common amongst hedgehogs. Similar to MS, it is fatal and there is no cure. While studies are ongoing, there is no known cause although many believe that it is genetic. It cannot be diagnosed for certain while the hedgehog is still alive, a necropsy MUST be performed to confirm. Caring for a hedgehog with this disease is time-consuming and heartbreaking. There are, however, many things that can be done to provide a good quality of life for an affected hedgehog including a special diet and modifying their houses so that they can be mobile for as long as possible. Massage is a very important part of WHS care so this will also be addressed. Our rescue station has cared for "wobbly hogs" and we would like to share everything that we have learned about palliative care for these little ones. Anyone who has experienced this also knows that an incredibly close bond will be built between owner and hedgehog.

Thanks for reading and we hope that in the future you will find this sub to be helpful!
Please feel free to introduce yourself and tell us what you would like to see here. Perhaps you have information you'd like to contribute yourself :)
